FRG-135 — a write rule on a system_only model

Trigger. A model marked #[ferra(system_only)] declares a create, update, delete or restore rule in its #[authorize] block. Ferra serves none of the four for such a model: it registers no route and documents no operation, and a write through Resource<M> is refused like an operation without a rule (403 with an identity, 401 without). Only a system grant writes it. A rule for an operation that does not exist would look like a posture and do nothing, so it is refused. The block asks for list and get only (FRG-101). Reported at the rule’s key.

A field’s #[field(write = ...)] rule is refused the same way: the model has no write route to gate, and the system grant’s insert ignores field rules. Reported at the field’s write key.

#[ferra(hooks)] is refused the same way, since 0.14.0: hooks run on a write, the model serves none, and the grant inserts without the target’s hooks, so they never ran. Reported at the hooks key. A model that writes through a grant declares hooks(system = T) on the hooked model, not on T.

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "audit_entries")]
#[ferra(system_only)]
#[authorize(list = Authenticated, get = Authenticated, create = Authenticated)] // `create` is not served
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i64,
    pub action: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]

    #[field(write = HasRole("admin"))] // no write route to gate

FRG-136 — a relation target or an owner(from) parent that is not a Ferra model

Trigger. A relation field (BelongsTo, HasOne or HasMany) whose target Entity belongs to a model that does not derive FerraModel, or an owner(from = x) whose parent is such a model. Ferra reads the target’s metadata to build the relation and, for owner(from), to follow the chain to the parent’s owner, so the target must be a Ferra model. Reported at the relation field’s target type, and for owner(from) also at the from value. A parent that is not a model also draws FRG-127, which is true of it and needs no separate fix.

Bad.

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod context {
    use super::*;

    #[sea_orm::model]
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, Serialize, Deserialize)] // no `FerraModel`
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "contexts")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

mod source {
    use super::*;

    #[sea_orm::model]
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "sources")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        pub context_id: i32,
        #[sea_orm(belongs_to, from = "context_id", to = "id")]
        pub context: BelongsTo<super::context::Entity>,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}
fn main() {}

FRG-137 — groups has no effect

Trigger. The key groups is written, whatever its value: groups = ["admin"], groups = [], a bare groups, groups = "admin". It is refused on a field (#[ferra(groups = …)]), inside projection(...) and on the struct. Reported at the groups key.

Ferra does not scope fields by group. Until 0.14.0 the key was read and then dropped, so a field declared with it, groups = [] included, was served on every read and accepted in the default write body: a field believed restricted was served to everyone. A declaration that reads as a restriction must restrict, or not compile. #[field(groups = …)] is not a #[field(...)] key and keeps FRG-213; the typo group = [...] is the unknown-key error of #[ferra(...)], with a did you mean groups?.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "users")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(groups = [])]
    pub password_hash: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "users")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(write_only)]
    pub password_hash: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Say who may see or write the field in the way Ferra does:

  • read = [...] and write = [...] on a projection choose the fields of a shape;
  • #[field(read = …)] and #[field(write = …)] put a rule on one field;
  • #[ferra(skip)] keeps a field out of every response and write body, and #[ferra(write_only)] accepts it on write and never serves it.

See Migrating from 0.13 to 0.14.

Fixtures. frg_137_field_nonempty.rs. The other placements and values (bare, empty, a string, in a projection, on the struct, beside skip) are the unit tests frg_137_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/ferra_attrs.rs.

FRG-138 — an attribute where Ferra does not read it

Trigger. A Ferra attribute is written where the derive does not read it: #[field(...)] on the struct, or #[authorize(...)], #[behavior(...)] or #[operation(...)] on a field. Reported at the attribute path, whatever the attribute holds. The same attribute under the dense form #[sea_orm::model] is refused the same way. Where each namespace goes: Three attribute namespaces.

The compiler accepts every helper attribute the derive declares on the struct and on each field, so before 0.14.0 a misplaced one compiled and did nothing. A struct-level #[field(owner)] looked like the ownership marker and marked no field: the rows stayed readable by everyone the model’s rules let through (OWASP API1 and API3). A declaration that reads as a protection must protect, or not compile. #[operation(...)] on a field gets this code, not FRG-335: on a field the first problem is the place.

Bad.

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "notes")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[field(owner)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub owner_id: i32,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "notes")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[field(owner)]
    pub owner_id: i32,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Move the attribute where it is read, or remove it:

  • #[field(...)] goes on the field it describes;
  • #[authorize(...)] and #[behavior(...)] go on the struct; a rule for one field is #[field(read = …, write = …)];
  • #[operation(...)] goes nowhere: add the route yourself with .route(...) (custom handlers).

See Migrating from 0.13 to 0.14.

Fixtures. frg_138_field_on_struct_dense.rs (the dense #[sea_orm::model] form, which needs the real macro). The plain struct and the field cases are the unit tests frg_138_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/parse.rs.

FRG-150 — mounting a model without posture

Trigger. Two sites share this code.

  • Compile time, at Foundry::mount::<M>() (and mount_and_handle, mount_with_layer): M does not implement the marker trait FerraAuthConfigured. #[derive(FerraModel)] implements it for every model that declares a posture, and stops a model without one earlier, at FRG-100 — so only a hand-written FerraModel impl reaches this error.
  • Run time, in Foundry::build(): a mounted model leaves one of the operations it serves without a rule. build() panics and the server does not start. Only a hand-written ModelMeta (or a hand-written FerraAuthConfigured impl) can get there.
error[E0277]: FRG-150: `Film` has no declared authorization posture, but `Foundry::mount::<Film>()` requires one — deny by default

thread 'main' panicked at …:
FRG-150: the model `Film` has no authorization rule for the `list` operation — Ferra refuses to serve an operation it cannot authorize (deny by default). …

No example. The compile-time site needs a type that implements FerraModel by hand without implementing FerraAuthConfigured; the constructors of the model description (ModelMeta, FieldMeta) are #[doc(hidden)] in 0.9.0, so an application cannot write one, and the run-time site needs a hand-written ModelMeta too. The code is defense in depth behind FRG-100: #[derive(FerraModel)] stops a model without a posture before it reaches Foundry::mount. The fixture pins the message with a stand-in type.

What mounting a model with a posture looks like:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")] // or "bearer", or an `#[authorize(...)]` block
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) {
let app = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).mount::<Model>().build();
}
}

Fix. Derive FerraModel and declare a posture on the model (see FRG-100). Do not implement FerraAuthConfigured by hand: it is a declaration that the model has a rule for every operation, and build() checks it.

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_mount_without_auth_configured.rs (compile time). The run-time panic is covered by the unit tests of crates/ferra-http/src/foundry.rs and crates/ferra-http/src/policy.rs.

FRG-151 — mounting without .with_auth() a model that needs an identity

Trigger. .mount::<M>() on a Foundry chain that has no .with_auth::<YourClaims>(jwt), where some rule of M needs an identity. With an #[authorize] block, that is any rule naming a checker other than Anyone; without a block, that is #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]. A projection’s authorize and a field’s read or write rule count too (0.13.0): a public model (auth = "none") with a projection or a field asking for Authenticated or a role needs .with_auth() as well. So does a #[ferra(me)] model, whatever its rules say: GET /me compares the caller with the owner, so the model needs an identity (a FRG-131 model has a unique owner for it). Such a model could never authorize a caller: without a JWT configuration nothing turns a token into an identity. The error points at the mount call:

error[E0277]: FRG-151: `Film` requires an identity, but this `Foundry` chain has no `.with_auth()`
   |     let app = Foundry::new(conn).mount::<Film>().build();
   |                                  ^^^^^ `Film` cannot be mounted without a JWT configuration
   = help: the trait `AuthGate<Film>` is not implemented for `NoAuth`

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
use ferra::{ClaimCheck, FerraIdentity, HmacAlgorithm, JwtConfig};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct MyClaims { sub: String }
impl FerraIdentity for MyClaims {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.sub }
    fn has_role(&self, _role: &str) -> bool { false }
}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let jwt = JwtConfig::single_secret(
    "key-1",
    std::env::var("JWT_SECRET")?,
    HmacAlgorithm::Hs256,
    ClaimCheck::expect("https://auth.example.com/"),
    ClaimCheck::expect("films-api"),
)?;
let app = ferra::Foundry::new(conn)
    .with_auth::<MyClaims>(jwt) // MyClaims: FerraIdentity + Deserialize
    .mount::<Model>()
    .build();
Ok(())
}
}

.mount_and_handle::<M>() has the same gate, so the same error:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) {
let (foundry, films) = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).mount_and_handle::<Model>(); // no `.with_auth()`
}
}

Fix. Call .with_auth::<YourClaims>(jwt) on the chain before the first .mount (it is not available once a model is mounted; before or after .api_version("v1")? makes no difference). If the model is deliberately public, declare #[ferra(auth = "none")] or make every rule Anyone instead — such a model mounts on any chain. ClaimCheck, JwtConfig and HmacAlgorithm are imported from ferra (they are not in ferra::prelude).

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_sec_004_bearer_without_with_auth.rs, and fail_mount_and_handle_without_auth.rs for mount_and_handle.

FRG-152 — a route of your own without the resource handle

Trigger. A handler takes Resource<M> but the router state it runs on holds no ResourceHandle<M>: the handle was never issued (the model was mounted with .mount::<M>(), or not mounted), or it was not put in the state. The handle is how a route reaches the rows of a model under the model’s rules; only .mount_and_handle::<M>() issues one. The error points at the Resource<M> argument of the handler. Add #[axum::debug_handler] to the handler to get it (it needs axum with its macros feature): without it axum reports its own, opaque, “the trait Handler<…> is not implemented”, and says so.

error[E0277]: FRG-152: `()` carries no `ResourceHandle<Film>`
   |     async fn mine(_films: Resource<Film>) {}
   |                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ no handle for `Film` in this state
   = note: mount `Film` with `.mount_and_handle::<Film>()` and keep the handle in your router state (a field of your state that derives `FromRef`).

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
#[axum::debug_handler(state = ())]
async fn mine(_films: ferra::Resource<Model>) {}
fn demo() {
let _app: axum::Router = axum::Router::new()
    .route("/films", axum::routing::get(mine))
    .with_state(()); // the state holds no `ResourceHandle<Model>`
}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
#[axum::debug_handler(state = ferra::ResourceHandle<Model>)]
async fn mine(_films: ferra::Resource<Model>) {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) {
let (foundry, films) = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).mount_and_handle::<Model>();
let _app: axum::Router = foundry
    .build()
    .merge(axum::Router::new().route("/films", axum::routing::get(mine)).with_state(films));
}
}

Fix. Mount the model with .mount_and_handle::<M>() instead of .mount::<M>(), and keep the handle it returns in the state of the router the handler is on: .with_state(handle) for a router of one model, or a field of your own state that derives axum::extract::FromRef.

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_resource_handle_missing.rs

FRG-153 — an OpenAPI name produced twice

Trigger. Foundry::build() finds an OpenAPI component name or operationId that the mounted models register twice, and panics: the server does not start. The document keys its schemas by name, so the second registration would overwrite the first without a word, and a client generated from the document would read a model, or a projection, through the shape of another. Both registrations can come from

  • one model: a projection x-collection, whose read schema has the name of the list envelope of a projection x (FilmXCollection), or a projection collection-hal, whose read schema has the name of the HAL form of the default list envelope (FilmCollectionHal);
  • two models: Film with a summary projection, and a model FilmSummary (FilmSummary, CreateFilmSummaryInput, getFilmSummary);
  • a projection and the shared error schema: a projection details of a model Problem produces ProblemDetails, the schema every error response references.

A projection’s schemas are {Model} then the PascalCase of its name, with the Create…Input, Update…Input, …Collection and …Hal forms. collection and hal are refused at compile time (FRG-317); this code covers every other pair of names, ProblemDetails included: Ferra registers it first, and a model or projection that produces it is the second owner.

Detection site. Foundry::build() reads the names where the document registers them, so it needs no .with_docs(). The operationIds are read in the whole document built, whatever the operation: CRUD, restore, /me, a projection’s.

The application refuses to start: Foundry::build() panics, before any route is served, with a one-line message about the first name it finds twice. The two lines below are two separate panics. The first is the FilmXCollection example above (x and x-collection of the model Film). The second comes from a ModelMeta written by hand instead of by the derive, which declares two actions named restore on Film, one at /restore and one at /restore-again.

FRG-153: the OpenAPI component `FilmXCollection` is produced twice, by projection `x` of the model `Film` and by projection `x-collection` of the model `Film`: the document would keep one and drop the other. Rename a projection (`#[ferra(projection(name = ...))]`) or a model's resource (`#[ferra(resource = ...)]`) so that the names differ. See docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-153.
FRG-153: the OpenAPI operationId `restoreFilm` is produced twice, by `POST /films/{id}/restore` (the model `Film`) and by `POST /films/{id}/restore-again` (the model `Film`): the document would keep one and drop the other. Rename a projection (`#[ferra(projection(name = ...))]`) or a model's resource (`#[ferra(resource = ...)]`) so that the names differ. See docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-153.

Bad (compiles; panics when build() runs).

#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[ferra(projection(name = "x", read = [id, title]))]
#[ferra(projection(name = "x-collection", read = [id, title]))] // `FilmXCollection` twice

Fix. Rename one of the projections, or give one of the two models another resource name (#[ferra(resource = "...")]), so that the names differ. The message names the name and its two sources, a model or a projection of a model, and for an operationId the two operations with their method and path.

Note on Class 4. Option<Uuid> was previously rejected outright by #[derive(FerraModel)] (Class 4 in ferra-forge.md § Troubleshooting). 0.6.0 Welding lifts the rejection — the type is now first-class — and replaces it with this narrower contradiction check. If you came here looking for the old “Option<Uuid> is not supported” diagnostic, that class is retired; the per-rule rejection above is the current diagnostic.

Compile-time diagnostic wrappers

Some Ferra attributes impose a trait bound on the field’s type — for example, #[ferra(computed)] requires the field’s type to implement Default (the framework supplies a compute-time placeholder by calling T::default()). When the bound is violated, rustc’s default message would be the language-level error[E0277]: the trait bound \T: Default` is not satisfied`. That phrasing is correct but tells the user nothing about why Ferra needs the bound or how to satisfy it in the Ferra-specific context.

To close that gap, ferra-core ships a small set of wrapper traits in ferra_core::diagnostics that re-export the underlying language traits under a framework-authored name and carry a #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented] annotation. The compiler reads the annotation and renders the framework’s message / label / note triple instead of its default E0277 text. The user sees a Ferra-shaped diagnostic on the first line of compiler output.

The shipped wrappers

Wrapper traitWrapped language traitConsumed by
FerraComputedDefaultDefault (blanket-impl’d for T: Default)ferra-forge’s compute_emit::emit_computed_bounds, once per #[ferra(computed)] field.
FerraSendSend (blanket-impl’d for T: Send + ?Sized)ferra-forge’s emit_bounds_assertion, once per field of the model, spanned at the field’s type. Ferra’s message appears when the field’s type is itself not Send (Rc<T>); for a struct that contains one, rustc names the inner type. Only a #[ferra(computed)] field can carry a type of yours: the classifier refuses any other type it does not know.
FerraSyncSync (blanket-impl’d for T: Sync + ?Sized)Sibling of FerraSend on the same per-field assertion (Cell<T> is Send and not Sync). Fixture: crates/ferra-forge/tests/ui/fail_non_sync_field.rs.
FerraAuthConfigurednone — a marker with no blanket implFoundry::mount::<M>() (FRG-150). #[derive(FerraModel)] implements it for every model that declares a posture.
FerraMountableWithoutAuthnone — a marker with no blanket implFoundry::mount::<M>() on a chain without .with_auth(), through the AuthGate<M> bound (FRG-151). #[derive(FerraModel)] implements it for a model none of whose rules needs an identity and that is not #[ferra(me)].

FerraComputedDefault, FerraSend and FerraSync wrap a language trait. FerraAuthConfigured and FerraMountableWithoutAuth wrap nothing: they are markers the derive writes for you, and the only fix for a missing one is on the model (or on the Foundry chain), never a hand-written impl. The two authorization markers are documented under FRG-150 and FRG-151. HoldsResource, the sealed trait behind FRG-152, is the same kind: a bound with a message, and nothing to implement.

The canonical diagnostic shape

The compiler renders a #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented] failure as three lines anchored on the offending type. The message is the top-line error: …; the label is the inline span annotation pointing at the offending position; the note is the bottom-line fix hint. For FerraComputedDefault:

error: `NotDefault` does not implement `Default`, but it is required for fields marked `#[ferra(computed)]`
  --> src/model.rs:LL:CC
   |
LL |     pub total: NotDefault,
   |                ^^^^^^^^^^ this type must implement `Default` for ferra-forge to supply its compute-time placeholder
   |
   = note: add `#[derive(Default)]` on `NotDefault`, or provide an explicit `impl Default for NotDefault`.

The framing — is required for fields marked \#[ferra(…)]`plus the explicitferra-forgereference in thelabel— is how a consumer (human or AI) recognises a Ferra wrapper diagnostic versus a generic rustc message. Whenever you see one of these triples, thenote:line names the fix verbatim; apply it on the offending type and re-runcargo check`.

Migration when an upgrade introduces a new wrapper-trait bound

Future Ferra releases land additional bounds (e.g. FerraAuthConfigured at 0.8.0). When an upgrade triggers a previously-passing compile to fail with a new wrapper-trait diagnostic:

  1. Recognise the framing. The message line names a Ferra attribute or generation context (required for fields marked \#[ferra(…)]`, FRG-150: … has no declared authorization posture`, …) rather than a bare language trait.
  2. Read the note: line. It names the concrete fix — a missing #[derive(...)], a missing impl, or a missing attribute on the model.
  3. Apply the fix at the named site. The diagnostic’s --> path:LINE:COL anchor points at the exact source position; the wrapper-trait substrate guarantees the fix is local to the type or the model under the cursor.

The per-code FRG-3NN sections below cite individual diagnostics; the wrapper-trait substrate is shared by every emission that imposes a typed bound on user fields (the FerraComputedDefault consumer site is documented under FRG-3NN — computed/projection codes that share the wrapper substrate).

Computed-field default-value diagnostic

A #[ferra(computed)] field is computed by the framework at serialise time. The default emission strategy substitutes T::default() for the field’s value when reading the entity off the database — so the field’s type must implement Default. The proc-macro emits a bound assertion through the FerraComputedDefault wrapper trait (see Compile-time diagnostic wrappers) so the diagnostic surfaces the framework-authored triple instead of rustc’s generic E0277 text.

Bad — a user-named type that does not implement Default.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use ferra::compute::FerraComputed;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use sea_orm::DeriveValueType;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// A user-defined newtype that deliberately omits `#[derive(Default)]`.
/// Every other trait Ferra's substrate requires (`Clone`, `Debug`,
/// `PartialEq`, sea-orm's `ValueType` family via `DeriveValueType`,
/// serde derives) is in place — `Default` is the only missing piece.
#[derive(
    Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveValueType, Serialize, Deserialize,
)]
pub struct NotDefault(pub i64);

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(computed)]
    pub custom: NotDefault,
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
impl FerraComputed for Model {}
}

The diagnostic the developer sees — the framework-authored FerraComputedDefault #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented] triple, pinned verbatim by the trybuild golden crates/ferra-forge/tests/ui/computed_default_missing.{rs,stderr}:

error[E0277]: `NotDefault` is used as the type of a `#[ferra(computed)]` field, but it does not implement `Default`
  --> src/model.rs:LL:CC
   |
LL |     pub custom: NotDefault,
   |                 ^^^^^^^^^^ this type needs `impl Default for NotDefault`
   |
   = note: A `#[ferra(computed)]` field's type must implement `Default`: add `#[derive(Default)]` to the type or write `impl Default` for it. A model with a computed field must also write an `impl FerraComputed` for itself (an empty one when nothing is overridden), or `Foundry::mount` does not compile; see `docs/user-guide/ferra-forge.md#computed-fields`. Diagnostic emitted by `ferra_core::diagnostics::FerraComputedDefault`.
   = note: required for `NotDefault` to implement `FerraComputedDefault`
help: consider annotating `NotDefault` with `#[derive(Default)]`

Fix. Add #[derive(Default)] (or an explicit impl Default) on the field’s underlying type:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use sea_orm::DeriveValueType;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(
    Default, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveValueType, Serialize, Deserialize,
)]
pub struct NotDefault(pub i64);
}

The build now succeeds and the wrapper-trait bound is satisfied via the blanket impl impl<T: Default> FerraComputedDefault for T {} on [ferra_core::diagnostics::FerraComputedDefault].

FR-043 — non-computed fields are unaffected. A user-named field type that does NOT carry #[ferra(computed)] is rejected by the classifier cascade (type … is not supported by Ferra). The classifier widening that admits NotDefault above lives behind the #[ferra(computed)] gate by design; the negative control unit test frg_003_non_computed_user_named_rejected of crates/ferra-forge/src/classify.rs pins this invariant.

Multi-segment paths (module::MyType) are not admitted at 0.7.0. Only single-ident user-named types pass the gate. A path-qualified type continues to be rejected by the classifier cascade even under the computed gate. Use a use module::MyType as MyType; at the declaration site to surface the bare ident if the wrapper-trait diagnostic is desired.

FRG-3NN — projection-attribute diagnostics (0.6.5 Chasing)

The 0.6.5 Chasing release opens the FRG-3NN block for projection / computed / write-only attribute rejections. Codes FRG-301..FRG-312 and FRG-314 ship from the proc-macro parser (#[derive(FerraModel)]); codes FRG-312 and FRG-315 are runtime-detected at Foundry::build() and ship their full integration-test fixture when the corresponding API surface (cross-model collision check, nested-mounting) wires in. FRG-313 is intentionally unallocated — the slot is reserved for namespace stability; the framework will not recycle the identifier.

See Projections and routing for the user-facing contract; this page documents the compile-time enforcement.

FRG-301 — projection references an unknown field

Trigger. A #[ferra(projection(... read = [...]))] or write = [...] list contains an ident that does not match any field on the host struct. The check also fires when an ident references a field but in the wrong half (e.g. a #[ferra(write_only)] field listed in a read = [...]; see FRG-305 for that refinement).

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[ferra(projection(name = "admin", read = [ghost_field]))]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

FRG-302 — write_only and read_only on the same field

Trigger. A field carries both #[ferra(write_only)] and #[ferra(read_only)]. The two flags are mutually exclusive: a write-only field is inbound-only (e.g. a password on registration), a read-only field is outbound-only (e.g. a server-set timestamp); combining them produces a field that can be neither read nor written — a field nobody can interact with. Diagnostic span on the second-encountered flag.

Bad.

    #[ferra(write_only)]

FRG-303 — write_only and computed on the same field

Trigger. A field carries both #[ferra(write_only)] and #[ferra(computed)]. A computed field is server-produced — its value materialises at read time from other fields on the row — so it is strictly outbound. Tagging it write_only makes the field unreachable: the framework would never produce it on the read side and would reject inbound values on the write side. Diagnostic span on write_only.

FRG-304 — write_only on a primary-key field

Trigger. #[ferra(write_only)] on a field that also carries #[sea_orm(primary_key)]. Primary-key columns surface in _links.self.href and as /{resource}/{id} URL segments — they must round-trip on the read side. A write-only PK column would leave the inserted row structurally unaddressable. Composite-key models fire FRG-304 independently per PK column, so the developer resolves the full graph in one round-trip.

Bad.

    #[ferra(write_only)]
    pub workspace_id: i32,
    #[sea_orm(primary_key, auto_increment = false)]
    #[ferra(write_only)]
    pub document_id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

FRG-305 — write_only field appears in a read projection

Trigger. A field declared #[ferra(write_only)] is listed in some projection’s read = [...]. The structural exclusion of write-only fields from the read shape is the load-bearing security guarantee of US3 — there is no escape hatch via the projection attribute, even on an admin-scoped projection. Diagnostic span on the offending ident inside the read list.

FRG-306 — skip and non-empty groups on the same field

Retired in 0.14.0. From 0.6.5 to 0.13.x, a field that carried both #[ferra(skip)] and a non-empty #[ferra(groups = ["..."])] was refused with this code. groups never worked: the derive parsed it and dropped it, so a field with groups alone was served on every read and accepted in the default write body, as if the attribute were absent. Since 0.14.0 the key groups is refused whatever its value, so this code is never raised. The section stays as history, and the number is never recycled. The code that replaces it is FRG-137. To hide a field, use #[ferra(skip)] or #[ferra(write_only)]; to serve it only to some callers, name it in a projection’s read/write lists or give it a #[field(read = ...)] rule. If you see FRG-306, you are reading output from a Ferra release older than 0.14.0.

FRG-307 — legacy #[field(write_only)] form

Trigger. A field carries #[field(write_only)]. The #[field(...)] namespace is reserved for validation rules (FRG-201..FRG-215); write_only is a projection flag that lives under the #[ferra(...)] namespace per ADR-0006’s namespace harmonisation. The parser recognises the pre-ADR-0006 legacy spelling and emits FRG-307 with help pointing at the canonical #[ferra(write_only)] spelling.

FRG-310 — projection URL prefix collision

Trigger. Two projections on the same model produce the same URL prefix. Two failure shapes share this code:

  • Duplicate path_prefix. Two projections each declare the same literal path_prefix = "...", so both route to the same URL.
  • Double default = true. Two projections each carry default = true; both target the bare resource path (/{resource}/{id}) and therefore collide. The second default = true is the offending span.

The proc-macro detects single-model collisions at compile time; the framework’s Foundry::build() startup pass covers cross-model collisions as defense-in-depth (see FRG-312 for the projection-vs-resource case).

Bad (duplicate path_prefix).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]

FRG-311 — projection name is not a URL-safe segment

Trigger. A projection’s name = "..." cannot be normalised to a URL-safe segment (it contains characters outside [a-z0-9_-] after to_lowercase()) AND the projection does not supply an explicit path_prefix = "..." override. The framework needs a URL-safe segment to route the projection; when the name cannot produce one, the developer must either rename the projection or supply a path prefix verbatim.

FRG-312 — projection prefix collides with a resource route

Trigger. A projection’s auto-derived URL prefix collides with an existing resource route mounted elsewhere on the same Foundry. For example: model A is mounted at /admin, and model B declares a projection named admin — the projection would shadow the top-level resource at the shared URL prefix.

Detection site. This collision spans two models, so the proc-macro cannot see it at compile time (it parses one struct at a time). Detection lives at Foundry::build(): the runtime walks every registered resource route plus every projection prefix and panics on overlap with a FRG-312 error. The proc-macro emits no hint for this code.

Status at 0.6.5. The runtime collision check ships with the projection-routing wiring. A dedicated tests/diagnostics/frg_312_*.rs proc-macro fixture is intentionally absent — the diagnostic surface is runtime (a panic with the FRG-312 prefix), so the test lives as an integration assertion alongside other Foundry::build() checks rather than as a trybuild fixture.

FRG-315 — path_prefix declared on a sub-resource

Trigger. A model mounted as a sub-resource of another model (Foundry’s nested-mounting pattern) carries path_prefix = "..." on one of its #[ferra(projection(...))] declarations. The URL surface of a nested resource is governed exclusively by the root resource’s projection prefix (ADR-0030 §Nested resources); a sub-resource overriding the URL would break the one-prefix-per-request invariant.

Detection site. Primary detection lives at Foundry::build() time — the proc-macro cannot fully detect sub-resource context (it sees one struct at a time). The proc-macro carries a hint emit at the path_prefix attribute as defense-in-depth.

Status at 0.6.5. The framework’s nested-mounting API ships in a future release. The FRG-315 namespace slot and the parser hint are in place; the runtime fixture lands when nested-mounting becomes wireable.

Status in 0.9.0: reserved, never emitted. Nested mounting does not exist in 0.9.0: Foundry has no way to mount a model under another one, so no model is a sub-resource and nothing raises this code. There is no example to compile, and no fixture. The number stays allocated for the day nested mounting lands.

FRG-316 — default = true requires promotes_from + breaking_change_version

Trigger. Three triggers, one code:

  • A projection declares default = true without both promotes_from = "..." and breaking_change_version = "..." attestations on the same declaration. Setting default = true replaces the bare-path response shape — a silent breaking change to the public API contract (consumers continue requesting /{resource}/{id} and receive a different schema). The two attestations force the change to be visible in the source. Reported at default = true.
  • A projection declares promotes_from without default = true (0.14.0). The attestation says what a promoted projection replaces; on any other projection it was read and dropped. Reported at the promotes_from key.
  • The value of promotes_from is neither "auto-derived" nor "named:<name>" with <name> another projection declared in the same model (0.14.0): "named:ghost" for a projection that does not exist, "v1" for a name written without named:, and the projection’s own name (a projection was not its own previous default). Reported at the value.

Why both are required. promotes_from names what is being replaced ("auto-derived" for the framework’s default, or "named:<other>" for a previous named-default projection). The macro checks the value against the projections the model declares, anywhere in the model, and never against repository history: a former named default that you removed in the same change can no longer be named (use "auto-derived"). breaking_change_version surfaces in the OpenAPI document as the x-ferra-promoted-in: "X.Y.Z" vendor extension on every operation under the bare resource path, so SDK consumers and downstream tooling can detect the silent break.

Nothing compares a model’s bare-path default with an earlier build: a lockfile that would record each model’s default and a hash of its schemas, and fail the build on a drift, is not planned. The two attributes above are the only protection, so a copied attestation that nobody re-read is not caught.

FRG-317 — a reserved projection name

Trigger. #[ferra(projection(name = "default", ...))], name = "collection" or name = "hal". default names the model’s own read and write shapes, served at the bare path. collection and hal are reserved since 0.14.0: a projection’s read schema in the OpenAPI document is {Model} then the PascalCase of its name, so they would overwrite the model’s own list envelope {Model}Collection and HAL read {Model}Hal. Reported at the name.

FRG-323 — a field has the name of a column a behavior owns

Trigger. The struct declares a field whose name, or whose #[sea_orm(column_name = "...")], is a column a behavior it enrolls in owns: deleted_at with #[behavior(soft_delete)], created_at or updated_at with #[behavior(timestampable)], created_by or updated_by with #[behavior(blameable)], or the names given in #[behavior(...)] (soft_delete(column = "removed_at"), blameable(updated_by = "editor")). The error is at the field and names the behavior column.

Why. Each enrolled behavior adds a field named after its column to the model’s metadata. A field of yours with that name, or stored in that column through #[sea_orm(column_name = "...")], would claim the same column a second time: the behavior and your struct would both own it. Ferra refuses it at the field, and the message says whether the clash is the Rust name or the column_name.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
    pub deleted_at: Option<String>, // the behavior adds this column itself
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)] // adds `deleted_at`
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Remove the field: the behavior reads and writes that column itself, and the stamps and nothing else of it reach the clients. If you need a column of that name for something else, name the behavior’s column differently in #[behavior(...)]. If the clash is through column_name, change the field’s column_name instead, or the behavior’s column.

Fixture. crates/ferra-forge/tests/diagnostics/frg_323_behavior_field_conflict.rs (the span on the field’s identifier). The other clashes (a configured column, a blameable default or configured column, a #[sea_orm(column_name)]) point at the same token: the unit tests frg_323_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/parse.rs.

FRG-330 to FRG-334 — retired

These codes described the grammar of #[operation(path = ..., method = ...)]: a missing key, an unknown key, a / in the path, an unsupported method, a duplicate operation name. The attribute itself is refused since 0.9.0 (FRG-335), so none of them can fire any more. They are kept here as history and their numbers will not be reassigned. If you see one, you are reading output from a Ferra release older than 0.9.0.

FRG-330 — retired (missing #[operation] key)

See FRG-335.

FRG-331 — retired (unknown #[operation] key)

See FRG-335.

FRG-332 — retired (/ in #[operation(path)])

See FRG-335.

FRG-333 — retired (unsupported #[operation(method)])

See FRG-335.

FRG-334 — retired (duplicate operation name)

See FRG-335.

FRG-335 — #[operation(...)] is refused

Trigger. #[operation(...)] on a model, whatever its content. Before 0.9.0 the attribute produced a HAL link and an OpenAPI entry, but no route and no authorization rule: clients were told about an endpoint that answered 404. Reported at the operation attribute name.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)]
#[operation(path = "publish", method = "POST")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)] // still mounts POST /films/{id}/restore
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
use axum::{Json, Router, routing::post};
use ferra::{FerraError, FerraIdentity, Foundry, JwtConfig};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct MyClaims { sub: String }
impl FerraIdentity for MyClaims {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.sub }
    fn has_role(&self, _role: &str) -> bool { false }
}
async fn publish_film() -> Result<Json<()>, FerraError> { Ok(Json(())) }
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection, jwt: JwtConfig) {
// The action route is yours, added to the router `Foundry::build()` returns:
let (builder, films) = Foundry::new(conn)
    .with_auth::<MyClaims>(jwt)
    .mount_and_handle::<Model>();
let app = builder.build().merge(
    Router::new()
        .route("/films/{id}/publish", post(publish_film))
        .with_state(films),
);
}
}

Fix. Remove the attribute. restore is the only named operation: it is mounted by #[behavior(soft_delete)] and governed by the restore key of #[authorize]. Write any other action route yourself and add it with .route(...) or .merge(...) on the value Foundry::build() returns (see custom-handlers.md). Ferra’s authorization does not cover a route you add: protect it yourself, as that page shows.

FRG-340 — base_path has no leading slash

Trigger. FerraLayer::base_path("api"): the prefix does not start with /. Unlike the other codes of this page, this one is not raised by the derive but by an assert! in a const fn, and the message of the panic starts with the code: FRG-340: FerraLayer::base_path: the prefix must start with '/'. Called in a const (the usual place, const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = …), it is a compile error (“evaluation panicked”) at the literal; called in ordinary code, it panics when the line runs, which is at startup.

Bad.

}

use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("/api").build();
}

}

Bad.

const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("").build(); // empty
}

Good.

const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().build(); // no prefix
}

FRG-350 — #[field(filterable)] / #[field(sortable)] on a #[ferra(skip)] field

Trigger. A field declares #[field(filterable)] or #[field(sortable)] AND #[ferra(skip)] on the same declaration. The two markers contradict: #[ferra(skip)] removes the field from the API surface entirely (it does not appear in OpenAPI, requests, or responses), so a request cannot mention it as a filter or sort key — there is no surface to address. Per spec 011 FR-003, the framework refuses to compile a model that puts the field in both categories.

Why compile-time. The contradiction is decidable from the field’s declaration alone — no runtime input is needed. Constitution §III “Compile-Time over Runtime” forbids runtime checks for invariants the compiler can lift.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(skip)]
    #[field(filterable)] // contradicts skip: the field is not exposed
    pub internal_note: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix — expose the field.

Drop #[ferra(skip)] if the field should be exposed as a filterable column:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[field(filterable)]
    pub note: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix — keep the field internal.

Drop the filterable / sortable marker if the field should remain a server-internal column:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(skip)]
    pub internal_note: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Trigger. #[field(cursor_key)] on a field whose type is not Id, Uuid, i64, ferra::DateTime, ferra::Date or ferra::Time (for example a String, whose order is a collation and not a position). The error is at the field.

Bad.

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;

    #[field(cursor_key)]
    pub title: String, // a `String` has no total order the cursor can resume from
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

    #[field(cursor_key)]

    pub title: String,
}

Trigger. #[field(cursor_key)] on an Option<T> field, or on a tuple with an Option<T> component. A row whose key is NULL has no place in the keyset order: the traversal would skip it without a word. The error is at the field.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]

Fix. Remove the query markers: a JSON document is stored and returned, never filtered, sorted or walked by cursor; put the bounds in json(max_depth = .., max_bytes = ..). See ferra-core.md § JSON documents.

FRG-356 — a projection hides the cursor key or its tie-break key

Trigger. A model in cursor or both pagination mode has a projection whose read = [...] leaves out the #[field(cursor_key)] field, or the single primary key that breaks ties between equal cursor keys; or its cursor key is #[ferra(skip)] (and not the primary key), which the default read projection drops. The cursor token carries both values, so a projection that hides them would hand the client a field it cannot otherwise read. A write-only cursor key is FRG-354; this code is for a readable field that a projection omits. Reported at the cursor-key field, naming the projection and the field.

Bad.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none", pagination = "cursor")]
#[ferra(projection(name = "summary", read = [id, title]))] // `rank` is left out
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[field(cursor_key, sortable)]
    pub rank: i64,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]

FRG-358 — a read projection names a skipped field

Reported at the identifier in read, naming the projection and the field. The deletion column of a soft-delete model is skip too, and is FRG-357; FRG-305 is the same rule for a write-only field.
