OpenAPI names: some models, every list operation and every named projection change

Before. The name Ferra gives a model in the OpenAPI document, the root of its schema names and operation ids, is the singular of its resource name. It read movies as Movy, buses as Buse, gases as Gase, statuses as Statuse, viruses as Viruse, bonuses as Bonuse, cookies as Cooky and zombies as Zomby: the model Movie was published as Movy, CreateMovyInput, getMovy… The list operation id was the model name and an s (listFilms), so a model whose resource name is made with ies or es had a list id its resource name does not spell: listCategorys, listBoxs, listClasss.

After. Three changes, all in the document only. Routes, paths, tags and resource names do not change: /movies is still /movies.

  1. The eight plurals above are read as Movie, Bus, Gas, Status, Virus, Bonus, Cookie and Zombie, in any segment of a resource name (film_movies is FilmMovie, it was FilmMovy). Every other name is read as before.
  2. The list operation id is list and the plural of the model name, made the way the derive makes a resource name: a trailing y after a consonant becomes ies, a trailing s, x, z, sh or ch takes es, anything else takes s. listFilms stays, listCategorys becomes listCategories.
  3. A named projection is named after its model: {Model}{Projection}, the model being the singular of the resource name (the one #[ferra(resource = "...")] gives, else the default resource name). It was named after the Rust struct, which is Model in every Sea-ORM entity: the summary projection of Film was published as ModelSummary, CreateModelSummaryInput, UpdateModelSummaryInput, ModelSummaryCollection (and the HAL ones), and two models that named a projection alike shared one schema, the last mounted overwriting the other’s in components: a protected route could document another model’s fields. The projection’s operation ids were the default’s (getFilm twice); they now carry the projection (getFilmSummary). Schemas and operation ids of the default projection do not change.

Migration. A client generated from the document sees the renames. To spot them, list the keys of components.schemas and the operationIds of the document of the old and the new version, and compare: the generated client has the matching types and methods under the new names. Regenerate the client and rename its imports and calls. Every operation id that changes, by kind of model:

Kind of modelWasIs
Regular (Film, Actor)nothing changesnothing changes
In a consonant and y (Category, Story)listCategorys, listStoryslistCategories, listStories
In s, x, z, sh, ch (Class, Box, Watch)listClasss, listBoxs, listWatchslistClasses, listBoxes, listWatches
Movie (movies)getMovy, createMovy, updateMovy, deleteMovy, listMovysgetMovie, createMovie, updateMovie, deleteMovie, listMovies
Cookie (cookies)getCooky, createCooky, updateCooky, deleteCooky, listCookysgetCookie, createCookie, updateCookie, deleteCookie, listCookies
Zombie (zombies)getZomby, createZomby, updateZomby, deleteZomby, listZombysgetZombie, createZombie, updateZombie, deleteZombie, listZombies
Bus (buses)getBuse, createBuse, updateBuse, deleteBusegetBus, createBus, updateBus, deleteBus
Gas (gases)getGase, createGase, updateGase, deleteGasegetGas, createGas, updateGas, deleteGas
Status, Virus, Bonus (statuses, viruses, bonuses)getStatuse, createStatuse, updateStatuse, deleteStatuse (and Viruse, Bonuse)getStatus, createStatus, updateStatus, deleteStatus (and Virus, Bonus)

listBuses, listGases, listStatuses, listViruses and listBonuses do not change: the old id and the new one are the same word. The schema names follow the model name, so a renamed model also renames its schemas:

WasIs
Movy, CreateMovyInput, UpdateMovyInput, MovyCollectionMovie, CreateMovieInput, UpdateMovieInput, MovieCollection
Buse, CreateBuseInput, UpdateBuseInput, BuseCollectionBus, CreateBusInput, UpdateBusInput, BusCollection

(Gase, Statuse, Viruse, Bonuse, Cooky and Zomby follow the same pattern.) A model whose name is a regular singular (Film, Category, Class) keeps all its schema names and its get, create, update and delete ids.

A named projection summary of the model Film (resource films):

WasIs
ModelSummary, CreateModelSummaryInput, UpdateModelSummaryInput, ModelSummaryCollectionFilmSummary, CreateFilmSummaryInput, UpdateFilmSummaryInput, FilmSummaryCollection
getFilm, createFilm, updateFilm, deleteFilm, listFilms (the default’s)getFilmSummary, createFilmSummary, updateFilmSummary, deleteFilmSummary, listFilmsSummary
restoreFilm (a soft-delete model)restoreFilmSummary

The rename is on the schemas and the operation ids of projections that were published as Model...; a client that used one has the types and methods under the new names after regeneration.

A projection named collection or hal is a compile error (FRG-317)

Before. FRG-317 refused the projection name default only. A projection named collection or hal compiled, and in 0.13 its schemas did not clash with the model’s: they were named after the Rust struct (Model, see the section above), so its read schema was ModelCollection or ModelHal, not the model’s own list envelope FilmCollection or HAL read FilmHal.

After. FRG-317 refuses collection and hal as it refuses default, spanned on the name. The message lists the three reserved names and says which schema each would overwrite.

Migration. Rename the projection (summary, compact, public), and regenerate the client if it used the projection’s schemas: the new names follow the rule of the section above (FilmSummary).

Foundry::build() panics on an OpenAPI name produced twice (FRG-153)

Before. In 0.13 the schemas of a projection were named after the Rust struct (ModelSummary, see the section above), so a projection never collided with a model’s own names. Two cases did collide in schema names. Two mounted models that each declared a projection summary both produced ModelSummary, CreateModelSummaryInput, UpdateModelSummaryInput, ModelSummaryCollection (and the HAL ones). Inside one model, a projection x-collection next to x produced ModelXCollection twice (the list envelope of x, the read schema of x-collection). The document kept the last schema registered under a name and dropped the other, so a route could document the fields of another model or projection. No data was exposed. The operationIds of a projection were also the default’s (getFilm twice).

The 0.14.0 naming, {Model}{Projection}, adds collisions that 0.13 did not have, and build() now refuses them as well: Film with a summary projection and a model FilmSummary both produce FilmSummary and getFilmSummary; a projection collection-hal produces FilmCollectionHal, the HAL form of the default list envelope; a projection details of a model Problem produces ProblemDetails, the shared error schema.

After. build() panics before the server starts, as it does for FRG-310 and FRG-312, with a message that carries the code FRG-153, the name, its two sources (a model, or a projection of a model) and, for an operationId, the two operations with their method and path, for example FRG-153: the OpenAPI component `FilmXCollection` is produced twice, by projection `x` of the model `Film` and by projection `x-collection` of the model `Film` . Its signature does not change. The check runs whether or not .with_docs() is on, and reads the operationIds of the whole document: CRUD, restore, /me and the projections’.

Migration. Rename the projection that takes the name (x-collection becomes y), or give one of two models another resource name (#[ferra(resource = "...")]), so that the names differ.

Before, in 0.13: build() returned and the document kept one ModelXCollection. In 0.14 the same model panics in build():

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[ferra(projection(name = "x", read = [id, title]))]
#[ferra(projection(name = "x-collection", read = [id, title]))] // `FilmXCollection` twice
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) {
let _app = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).mount::<Model>().build();
}
}

    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]

Migrating from 0.12 to 0.13

0.13.0 (Engraving) changes what a projection, a field and a response may say. Each entry below is a change that can stop a 0.12 application from compiling or alter an answer; read the entries, then update the application’s git dependency to v0.13.0. CHANGELOG.md lists every change.

A projection names the deletion column in read (FRG-357)

Before. read = [id, title, deleted_at] on a #[behavior(soft_delete)] model compiled, and the response silently carried neither the column nor an error.

After. It does not compile: FRG-357.

Migration. Remove the deletion column from read = [...]. The response is the same as before, since the column was never served.

A projection names a #[ferra(skip)] field in read (FRG-358)

Before. read = [id, title, audit_blob] with audit_blob declared #[ferra(skip)] compiled, and the projection’s routes served the field.

After. It does not compile: FRG-358.

Migration. Remove the field from read = [...] (the routes then stop serving it), or remove #[ferra(skip)] from the field if the API should serve it.

_links.restore is gone from served rows

Before. Every live row of a soft-delete model carried _links.restore.href, a link that answered 404 on that live row.

After. A served row has no restore link. restore is still a route and is still in the OpenAPI document.

Migration. Build {prefix}/{resource}/{id}/restore yourself, or read it from OpenAPI, and call it on a row you know was deleted. Do not derive it from _links.self, which can be absent (next entry).

_links.self and _links.collection can be absent

Before. Every item carried _links.self and _links.collection, and the HAL item schema required self.

After. _links.self is present only if the caller may GET the row, and _links.collection only if the caller may list the collection. A caller who may list but not read a row gets the row without self. The HAL item schema no longer requires self.

Migration. A client or a generated SDK that assumed self must handle its absence. Under a projection prefix the links now carry the prefix (a fix: they pointed at the bare path before).

A create the caller may not read answers 201 with no body

Before. A caller who may create but not GET the new row received the row (its id, its stamps) and a Location header, or 204 and Location under Prefer: return=minimal.

After. Such a caller receives 201 Created with no body and no Location, also under Prefer: return=minimal. An admitted caller keeps the representation, or 204 under return=minimal, and its Location is the self link of the row. This closes a leak (SEC-008 bis): the id and the server-set values of a row the caller may not read.

Migration. A client that creates and then reads the Location must be allowed to GET the row, or look the row up by other means. Allow get for the roles that create, if they should read what they create.

An update or a restore the caller may not read answers 204 with no body

Before. A caller who may PUT or restore a row but not GET it received the row (its id, its stamps, its author) in the 200.

After. Such a caller receives 204 No Content with no body, whatever Prefer asked, and the write is done. An admitted caller keeps the 200 with the row, or 204 under return=minimal. Preference-Applied: return=minimal is echoed only when return=minimal was asked. This closes the same leak as the create (SEC-008 bis).

Migration. A client that reads the answer of a PUT or a restore must be allowed to GET the row, or read it separately. Allow get for the roles that write, if they should read what they write. A hand-written route on Resource::update serves what it chooses.

A hand-written model must carry the hook slot

Before. A hand-written FerraModel (no derive) that satisfied Mountable could be mounted.

After. Mountable also requires the hidden hook slot FerraDraft, with a runner for its Hooks. The derive writes it for every model, so a derived model changes nothing.

Migration. Add to a hand-written, mounted model:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::ferra_core::hooks::{FerraDraft, NoHooks};

struct Film;

impl FerraDraft for Film {
    type Draft = ();
    type Hooks = NoHooks;
}
}

Draft = () also satisfies the bound Mountable puts on the draft (ApplyDraft for the entity’s active model, DeserializeOwned and Send). A model that is only derived needs nothing. Hand-writing a model is outside the contract, which is the derive (see stability.md).

A hand-written model must carry the authority traits

Before. A hand-written FerraModel (no derive) that satisfied Mountable could be mounted.

After. Mountable also requires FerraAuthority and the hidden FerraAuthorityScope. The derive writes both for every model (an authority that allows everything without #[ferra(authority)]), so a derived model changes nothing.

Migration. Add to a hand-written, mounted model:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::authority::{AuthorityError, FerraAuthority};
use ferra::condition::Condition;
use ferra::ferra_core::authority::FerraAuthorityScope;
use ferra::meta::Operation;
use ferra::request_context::RequestContext;

struct Film;

impl FerraAuthority for Film {
    fn can(_: &RequestContext, _: Operation, _: &Self) -> Result<bool, AuthorityError> {
        Ok(true)
    }
}

impl FerraAuthorityScope for Film {
    fn scope_filter(_: &RequestContext) -> Option<Result<Condition<Self>, AuthorityError>> {
        None
    }
}
}

Ok(true) and None are what the derive writes without #[ferra(authority)]: no authority, no condition. Hand-writing a model is outside the contract, which is the derive (see stability.md).

A hand-written model must carry the owner chain and the derived views

Before. A hand-written FerraModel could be mounted without FerraOwnerChain, and could implement FerraViews by hand.

After. Mountable also requires the hidden FerraOwnerChain, and FerraViews has a required hidden method read_object. The derive writes both, so a derived model changes nothing.

Migration. Add to a hand-written, mounted model without owner(from = ..):

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::ferra_core::meta::FerraOwnerChain;

struct Film;

impl FerraOwnerChain for Film {
    type Parent = Self;
    const FOREIGN_KEY: Option<&'static str> = None;
}
}

FerraViews cannot be written by hand any more: derive FerraModel. Hand-writing a model is outside the contract, which is the derive (see stability.md).

New: #[ferra(hooks)] (application code inside a write)

Nothing changes for a model that does not declare it. To run your own code inside the write’s transaction, add #[ferra(hooks)] to the model and write impl ferra::hooks::FerraHooks for Model (every hook has a default that does nothing). The key without the impl, and the impl without the key, are FRG-129; a key inside hooks(...) is FRG-132. before_save rewrites ModelDraft, which the derive writes for the model. See behaviors.md.

New: GET /me

Nothing changes for a model that does not declare it. To serve the caller’s own row at GET /me, add #[ferra(me)] to the model that has a unique root #[field(owner)] (#[sea_orm(unique)] on it, or the single-column primary key: FRG-131 otherwise) and mount it with .with_auth() (FRG-151 otherwise). One model per Foundry, and no model whose resource (its URL segment: the table_name, or #[ferra(resource = "...")]) is me: build() panics with a message that names the models. A .route("/me", ...) of your own now conflicts with it, and build() panics on that too. See projections-and-routing.md.

New: #[behavior(blameable)] (blame columns)

Nothing changes for a model that does not enrol it. To record who wrote a row, add #[behavior(blameable)] and two TEXT NOT NULL columns to the table (created_by, updated_by; the names are configurable). The migration, who may read the columns (read = <rule>, Authenticated by default) and the compile error for an operation an anonymous caller may call (FRG-121) are in behaviors.md. Give your identity type’s FerraIdentity::id() (conventionally the JWT sub, see ferra-auth.md) a verified, stable, non-empty value: a write with no subject is a 500 and nothing is written.

A projection widens exposure without authorize (FRG-117)

Before. A projection could list in read or write a field the bare path does not expose or accept, with nothing saying who may use it: its routes followed the model’s rules, as the bare path does.

After. It does not compile: FRG-117. A projection that shows or accepts less than the bare path, or the same, is unaffected, with one exception. If you promoted a projection to the bare path (default = true) and gave it an authorize rule, that rule protects the bare path only; every other projection of the model must then declare its own authorize (a rule, or inherit), whatever fields it shows.

Migration. Add authorize = <rule> to the projection (for example authorize = HasRole("editor") | IsAdmin; the rule grammar is in ferra-auth.md § Authorization rules): the rule is added to the model’s rule of each operation, and a caller it refuses gets a 404. If the model’s rules are enough, write authorize = inherit to keep the 0.12 behavior knowingly.

RequestContext is filled and is no longer Copy

Before. RequestContext was an empty Copy marker: let c = ctx; left ctx usable, and the type was UnwindSafe and RefUnwindSafe.

After. It carries the caller (subject(), is_authenticated(), has_role(), claims::<C>(), api_key()) and the request headers (header()). It owns an Arc and a header list, so it is Clone but no longer Copy, UnwindSafe or RefUnwindSafe. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and the Foundry’s API key header are dropped when it is built, so header() answers None for them and Debug prints the subject and the header names, never a value. Every other header is client-supplied (X-Forwarded-*, Host, Origin as sent). See ferra-core.md.

Migration. Code that copied a RequestContext (let c = *ctx;, a Copy bound, a const fixture used twice) calls .clone() instead. The FerraComputed signatures take &RequestContext and do not change. Code that moved one across catch_unwind needs AssertUnwindSafe.

Migrating from 0.11 to 0.12

0.12.0 changes what a response says to a cache, how a 401 reads, and how a declared route reads its caller. It adds three credential sources (an EdDSA key set, API keys, a cookie), which change nothing for an application that configures none of them. Read the table, then update the application’s git dependency to v0.12.0. CHANGELOG.md lists every change.

BeforeAfterMigration
A response without Cache-Control was cacheable by heuristicsEvery response carries Cache-Control: no-store, inserted only when the route set noneA public route opts back in with its own Cache-Control
Vary held Accept on negotiated responses onlyEvery response has a Vary merged with Accept, Authorization, Cookie (and the API key header when keys are configured)None; do not strip it in a CDN
per_page above 100 sent Warning: 214No Warning header; the body’s per_page is the applied valueCompare the body’s per_page with the value asked
A 401 detail named the Authorization: Bearer headerThe detail is “valid credentials are required to access this resource”Match on type, never on detail
JwtConfig::validate checked any configOnly a secrets config validates; on a key set it returns Err(TokenRejection::KidUnknown)Call it from tests with a secrets config; verification of a key set runs in the layer
An extractor-based .route handler was told to wrap the route in FerraAuthLayerPrincipal<I>, CurrentUser<I> and Resource<M> read the credential themselvesRemove the wrapper; I must be DeserializeOwned
The public ferra_auth_middleware and ferra_auth_enforcing_middleware read the first Authorization headerThey answer 400 multiple_credentials on two Authorization headersSend one credential per request
CurrentUser<I> and Resource<M> from_request_parts were synchronousThey are async fn; CurrentUser and Principal need I: DeserializeOwned.await a direct call; derive Deserialize on the claims type
filter[f][]=v was read as equality400 unsupported_operatorSend filter[f]=v or filter[f][eq]=v
A 401 or 403 from the auth layer carried no CORS headerA listed origin gets Access-Control-Allow-* on it (CORS wraps authentication)None; a browser app can now read these errors

Caching

no-store is the default because a shared cache must never serve one caller’s row to another. A route that is public on purpose sets its own header, and Ferra keeps it:

.route("/health", get(health).layer(SetResponseHeaderLayer::overriding(
    CACHE_CONTROL, HeaderValue::from_static("public, max-age=60"))))

A layer you add on the built Router can overwrite the header after Ferra; Ferra cannot see that. See Caching.

Declared routes and credentials

A handler declared with FoundryBuilder::route that takes Principal<I>, CurrentUser<I> or Resource<M> now answers 400 multiple_credentials, 401 and 503 identity_unavailable exactly as a model route does. A route that reads no caller reads no credential. Option<Principal<I>> is None only when no credential is sent. CurrentUser<I> stays token-only: it answers 401 on an API key request, so use Principal<I> when keys are configured. See Who is calling a declared route.

New sources, opt in

JwtConfig::key_set (an EdDSA key set fetched over HTTPS; one kind of JWT source per Foundry), FoundryBuilder::with_api_keys and JwtConfig::with_cookie are additions. With a key set, the request budget must be above the fetch timeout (3 s by default) or build() panics. The whole chain is described in Authentication.

New error types

multiple_credentials (400) and identity_unavailable (503) join the closed error set; a client that switches on type handles both as new members.

Migrating from 0.10 to 0.11

0.11.0 changes response representations, validation errors, query refusals and behavior read shapes. Update clients before changing the application’s git dependency to v0.11.0. CHANGELOG.md lists the changes.

Response representations

BeforeAfterMigration
Accept: application/json returned HAL with _linksIt returns flat JSON without _linksSend Accept: application/hal+json to keep links
HAL had Content-Type: application/jsonHAL has Content-Type: application/hal+jsonAccept this media type, including when sending no Accept
A cursor list exposed the next token through _links.nextBoth representations have required next_cursor, a string or nullFlat clients pass the token back with the original filters and sort
OpenAPI collection schemas included _linksThe flat schema excludes it; the HAL media type adds itRegenerate clients and select the intended media type
OpenAPI collection envelopes were closed objectsThey are open (additionalProperties)A generated client reads unknown members of a list instead of refusing them

No Accept, */*, an unusable header or equal quality values select the Foundry default, initially HAL. default_representation(Representation::Flat) changes that default before the first mount. Every negotiated successful response, including 204, carries Vary: Accept; 201 keeps Location. Errors remain application/problem+json in both representations.

HAL pagination links now preserve filters and sort. A client building its own cursor request must also preserve them; omit page and per_page beside cursor. See Response representations and Pagination.

Validation errors

A 422 previously grouped messages by field:

{"errors":{"title":["too short"]}}

It now uses one top-level array:

{"errors":[{"field":"title","code":"min_length","message":"too short"}]}

A 400 validation previously nested this array under errors.errors; it now uses the same top-level errors array. Query validation failures also carry an entry. The examples show the changed member; the surrounding problem document retains its status, type and title.

Branch on code, not message. Group entries by field if the interface needs the old map. Field names use their wire spelling after rename_all.

ValidationError.code and FerraError::BadRequest

ValidationError.code changes from &'static str to ValidationCode; ValidationError::new and ValidationErrors::single take that enum (as_str() is the wire value). FerraError::BadRequest gains field and code. See Validation codes.

Before:

use ferra::{FerraError, ValidationError, ValidationErrors};

let errors = ValidationErrors::single("title", "min_length", "too short");
let one = ValidationError::new("title", "min_length", "too short");
let refused = FerraError::BadRequest { detail: "sort: unknown field".into() };
if let FerraError::BadRequest { detail } = &refused { /* … */ }

After:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::{FerraError, ValidationCode, ValidationError, ValidationErrors};

let errors = ValidationErrors::single("title", ValidationCode::MinLength, "too short");
let one = ValidationError::new("title", ValidationCode::MinLength, "too short");
assert_eq!(one.code.as_str(), "min_length");
let refused = FerraError::BadRequest {
    detail: "sort: unknown field".into(),
    field: "sort".into(),
    code: ValidationCode::NotSortable,
};
if let FerraError::BadRequest { field, code, .. } = &refused {
    assert_eq!((field.as_str(), code.as_str()), ("sort", "not_sortable"));
}
}

Query parameters and cursors

BeforeAfterMigration
Repeated recognized parameters kept the last value400 duplicate_parameterSend each recognized parameter once
page=abc or per_page=abc used defaults400 invalid_parameterSend an integer or omit the parameter
Cursor tokens used v1New tokens use v2 and carry directionTreat tokens as opaque; ascending v1 tokens still work
A cursor walk was ascendingsort=-key permits descending walksRepeat the same sort when passing back the cursor

Duplicate checking happens after percent-decoding. filter[title] and filter[title][eq] are the same key, even with identical values. It covers filters, sort, page, per_page and cursor; unknown parameters are unchanged. Distinct comparison operators can form a date range.

Replaying an ascending cursor with descending sort is refused. Date query filters require UTC (Z or +00:00), uppercase T, no annotations; Time has no offset. This restriction is on query filters: request bodies still accept RFC 3339 offsets and normalize timestamps to UTC.

Named read projections on cursor-mode models must include the cursor key and its primary-key tie-breaker; otherwise FRG-356 points at the field. Add these fields to every read projection, or change the pagination posture.

CollectionParams.filter, CollectionQuery.filter, CursorQuery.filter

The field types are unchanged (BTreeMap<String, String>, keyed by the Rust name of the field): a key may now carry an operator, field[gt], field[gte], field[lt], field[lte] on a date field, and field is still eq. A CursorQuery also carries the direction of its walk; the struct is #[non_exhaustive], built by CursorQuery::new and its with_* methods, so a route of yours changes only when it wants a descending walk.

Before:

use ferra::{CollectionQuery, CursorQuery};

let page = CollectionQuery::new(1, 20).with_filter("year", "2001");
let walk = CursorQuery::new(20); // ascending, the only order

After:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::{CollectionQuery, CursorQuery, SortDirection};

let page = CollectionQuery::new(1, 20)
    .with_filter("year", "2001") // still `eq`
    .with_filter("released_at[gte]", "2001-01-01T00:00:00Z"); // a comparison, UTC
assert_eq!(page.filter.len(), 2);
let walk = CursorQuery::new(20).with_direction(SortDirection::Desc);
assert_eq!(walk.direction, SortDirection::Desc);
}

Behavior timestamps and deletion columns

Timestampable responses now include creation and update stamps when the read projection allows them. Their wire names follow rename_all.

BehaviorKind fields

BehaviorKind::SoftDelete and BehaviorKind::Timestampable carry the column names (deleted_at, created_at, updated_at unless the model names its own). The enum and both variants are #[non_exhaustive]: a match keeps its wildcard arm and ends a variant pattern with ..; BehaviorKind::soft_delete and BehaviorKind::timestampable build a value.

Before:

use ferra::meta::BehaviorKind;

fn deletion_column(kind: &BehaviorKind) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match kind {
        BehaviorKind::SoftDelete => Some("deleted_at"),
        _ => None,
    }
}

After:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::meta::BehaviorKind;

fn deletion_column(kind: &BehaviorKind) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match kind {
        BehaviorKind::SoftDelete { column, .. } => Some(column),
        BehaviorKind::Timestampable { .. } => None,
        _ => None,
    }
}
assert_eq!(deletion_column(&BehaviorKind::soft_delete("removed_at")), Some("removed_at"));
}

ModelMeta::soft_delete_column and ModelMeta::timestamp_columns read the names for you.

FerraViews read structs gain the two timestamps as Option<DateTime>. Conversion from the entity alone leaves them None; use the stamped view returned by Resource<M> to obtain database timestamps.

The deletion column leaves default read projections, OpenAPI read schemas and FerraViews read structs. Remove client references to that read member. Bodies containing creation, update or deletion stamps remain refused with 422 unknown_field; these values are managed by the database. See Behaviors.

Also new in 0.11.0, no migration

Additions a 0.10 application compiles against unchanged:

  • FerraLayer::new().no_rate_limit().build() turns the mutation limiter and its 429 mapper off; Foundry::rate_limit_key(RateLimitKey::forwarded_for(TrustedProxies::new(["10.0.0.0/8"])?)) keys the quota on the rightmost untrusted X-Forwarded-For entry, read only from a trusted peer; RateLimitKey::from_fn reads a key of your own. See Foundry § Rate-limit override.
  • Foundry::request_budget(Duration) answers 503 https://ferra.rs/errors/timeout when a request outlives its budget before its commit starts. FerraError::Timeout is a new variant of the #[non_exhaustive] enum: a match of yours already has the wildcard arm it needs; a client handling type URIs gets a twelfth one. See Foundry § Request budget.

Migrating from 0.9 to 0.10

0.10.0 removes every public path to a model’s rows that did not go through the model’s rules. The compiler finds each use: the removed items no longer resolve. CHANGELOG.md is the full list.

You usedWrite instead
FerraState<M> in a route’s state, state.repolet (builder, films) = Foundry::…mount_and_handle::<M>(); keep films (a ResourceHandle<M>) in your state; extract Resource<M> in the handler
.mount_with::<M>(state).mount::<M>(), or .mount_and_handle::<M>() when a route of your own needs the rows
PgRepository, FerraRepositoryResource<M> (get, list, list_cursor, create, update, delete): it applies the checkpoint, the owner scope and the validation the generated routes apply
DatabaseTransactionyour own DatabaseConnection (conn.begin()), outside Ferra’s contract
FerraDbErrorFerraError, which every Resource<M> method returns
prelude FerraStateprelude Resource

A read-only state.repo route

// 0.9
async fn count(State(repo): State<Arc<PgRepository<Film>>>) -> ... { repo.find_page(1, 1) ... }
// 0.10: through the model's rules
async fn count(films: Resource<Film>) -> Result<Json<u64>, FerraError> {
    Ok(Json(films.list(&CollectionQuery::new(1, 1)).await?.total))
}

Rows the caller may not see are not counted: that is the point. A query the access does not cover (a join, an aggregate) runs on your own connection, which no rule guards: see custom-handlers.md § Raw database access, outside the contract.

Migrating from 0.8 to 0.9

0.9.0 closes the security flaws the 2026-09 audit proved and freezes the public contract. It breaks on purpose, once. This page is the order to do things in; CHANGELOG.md is the full list. The compiler does most of the work: every removed attribute answers with an FRG- diagnostic that says what to write instead (ferra-forge-diagnostics.md).

1. The dependency

[dependencies]
ferra = { git = "https://github.com/ferra-rs/ferra", tag = "v0.9.0" }

Remove any direct dependency on ferra-core, ferra-db, ferra-http or ferra-openapi: the facade is the only Ferra crate you declare. Declare sea-orm yourself, with the same major version as Ferra (2.x) — the exact line is at the top of CHANGELOG.md — and write sea_orm::…; sea-orm-migration, if you have migrations, takes the same major. To declare nothing, write ferra::sea_orm::… instead, with use ferra::prelude::*; or use ferra::sea_orm; at the top of each file that uses a Sea-ORM derive. Rust 1.94 or later.

2. Each model

  1. Give it a posture: #[ferra(auth = "bearer")], or an #[authorize(...)] block that names every operation it serves (FRG-100). An operation the block does not name is refused.
  2. Remove projection(authorize = ...), #[ferra(exposure = ...)] and #[operation(...)] (FRG-105, FRG-106, FRG-335).
  3. Remove serde renames. For camelCase JSON, add #[ferra(rename_all = "camelCase")] (FRG-116).
  4. Replace chrono, time and jiff field types by ferra::DateTime, ferra::Date, ferra::Time.
  5. If clients send the primary key (a composite or natural key), add #[ferra(client_pk)]. Otherwise the server generates it, and a body that carries it is a 422: tell your clients.
  6. If rows are owned, mark the column #[field(owner)]: the server fills it from the token. Clients stop sending it.

3. The mount

use ferra::{ClaimCheck, HmacAlgorithm, JwtConfig};
use ferra::{FerraIdentity, FerraModel, Foundry};
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod film {
    use super::*;
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        pub title: String,
    }
    #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
    pub enum Relation {}
    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}
use film::Model as Film;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct MyClaims { sub: String }
impl FerraIdentity for MyClaims {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.sub }
    fn has_role(&self, _role: &str) -> bool { false }
}
async fn demo(
    conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection,
    listener: tokio::net::TcpListener,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let jwt = JwtConfig::single_secret(
    "key-1",
    std::env::var("JWT_SECRET")?, // at least 32 bytes for HS256
    HmacAlgorithm::Hs256,
    ClaimCheck::expect("https://auth.example.com/"),
    ClaimCheck::expect("films-api"),
)?;
let app = Foundry::new(conn)
    .with_auth::<MyClaims>(jwt)
    .mount::<Film>()
    .build();
axum::serve(listener, app.into_make_service_with_connect_info::<std::net::SocketAddr>()).await?;
Ok(())
}
fn main() {}
  • ferra_router(...) and the versioned builder are gone: one chain, with .with_auth, .api_version("v1")? and .layer(...) before the first .mount.
  • .deprecated(sunset) is .deprecated(since, sunset)?.
  • RateLimitRule::new(..) returns a Result.
  • Links are relative; call .with_base_url("https://api.example.com")? if your clients need absolute ones.

4. Your own routes

  • ItemResponse, CollectionResponse, PaginationParams and the link builders are gone. Answer with a struct of your own (custom-handlers.md).
  • Collection reads of the repository take a query value: repo.find_collection(&CollectionQuery::new(page, per_page)).
  • Add a wildcard arm where you match on FerraError or FerraDbError.
  • Know the caller in a route declared with .route(...): extract Principal<Claims>, CurrentUser<Claims> or Resource<M> (since 0.12.0 they read the credential themselves; wrapping the route in FerraAuthLayer is no longer needed).

5. Your tests

FerraState::with_mock_identity and the production-check feature are gone. Send a real token:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use serde::Serialize;
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Claims { sub: String, iss: String, aud: String, exp: u64 }
fn demo(secret: &str, claims: Claims) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let authorization = ferra::testing::bearer("key-1", secret, ferra::HmacAlgorithm::Hs256, &claims)?;
let _ = authorization;
Ok(())
}
}

The value is the whole Authorization header, Bearer … included.

6. Your clients

What a client sees0.80.9
Someone else’s row under IsOwner403404
A body field the server owns (key, owner, read_only)accepted422
Content-Type other than JSON on a writeaccepted415
Linksabsolute, from Hostrelative, or from with_base_url
A cursor issued before the upgrade—400 invalid_cursor: restart from the first page
sort=-key with a cursor200, ascending400
SunsetYYYY-MM-DDan HTTP date, with Deprecation

7. Check

One rule first: a project never holds two major versions of Sea-ORM, not even for its tests or an optional feature. If your Cargo.toml has sea-orm = "1" in [dev-dependencies] (for a MockDatabase, say) or behind a feature (full = ["dep:sea-orm"]) while a model goes through the facade, 0.8 compiled it and 0.9 refuses it with FRG-400 once the tests or the feature are on. Move that line to Ferra’s major (sea-orm = "2"), or remove it and use ferra::sea_orm.

cargo build until it compiles, then cargo tree -d -i sea-orm: it prints nothing when the build holds one copy of Sea-ORM (FRG-400 says so at compile time otherwise). Then run your tests against a database. From then on, upgrading is changing the tag, changing the sea-orm line if the changelog says to, and reading CHANGELOG.md (stability.md).
